chat_messages.text: My sourdough starter has stopped rising and smells like acetone. What is going wrong with it?
An acetone smell means the starter is hungry and has exhausted its food supply. Feed it twice daily at a one to one to one ratio until the smell fades and it doubles reliably.
How wet should the dough feel after the first mix, and does hydration change the crumb?
A seventy-five percent hydration dough feels tacky but releases from wet hands. Higher hydration opens the crumb but demands stronger gluten development through folds.
My loaves keep coming out flat instead of tall. Is my shaping technique the problem?
Flat loaves usually mean under-fermented dough or weak surface tension from shaping. Build tension by dragging the boule toward you on an unfloured patch of counter.
I want to buy my first telescope for viewing planets. Should I get a refractor or a reflector?
For planets a long focal-length refractor gives crisp high-contrast views with zero maintenance. A Dobsonian reflector gives more aperture per dollar if you also want faint galaxies.
What magnification do I actually need to see the rings of Saturn clearly?
Saturn's rings resolve clearly at around one hundred fifty times magnification on a steady night. The atmosphere limits most nights to two hundred times regardless of the eyepiece.
Is light pollution in a city a dealbreaker for planetary observing?
Planets are bright enough that city light pollution barely matters for them. Dark skies only become essential when you chase nebulae and galaxies.
